description: Capture an event involving exposed user credentials — paste-site dumps, breach data resold on a marketplace, an OSINT tip, or a notification from a service the org has accounts on. Designed to be filled fast: the headline is *which accounts* and *where they were seen*.
name: Credential exposure

structure.help: Who's reporting it and where it surfaced. The free-text `source_label` ends up in the event info field; pick something concise (e.g. *PasteBin Apr 2026*, *Breach: ACME 2025*, *HIBP notification*).
structure.label: Exposure overview

structure.help: Short tag for where this exposure came from. Used in the event info field. Free text, no need for a URL.
structure.label: Source label

structure.help: When you first saw this exposure (not when the underlying breach happened — that goes in the *Breach context* section if known). ISO 8601.
structure.label: Date observed

structure.help: One or two sentences orienting a reader who scans the events index. Detail belongs in an event report.
structure.label: Short incident summary

structure.help: URLs, Telegram channels, marketplace listings — wherever you observed the leak. At least one entry is strongly encouraged for traceability.
structure.label: Where the credentials were seen

structure.help: Best single URL pointing at the exposure (paste, marketplace listing, archive). Defang on copy if your tooling requires.
structure.label: Primary leak URL

misp.comment_template: Primary venue where the leak was observed

structure.help: Mirrors, re-uploads, related archives. One URL per entry.
structure.label: Additional leak URL

structure.help: What was actually exposed. Capture representative items rather than dumping every line — large lists belong in an attached file.
structure.label: Affected accounts

structure.help: Email address visible in the dump. Use **+ Add another instance** for multiple. If the list is long, attach the raw file as a *file_field* below instead of pasting line by line.
structure.label: Affected email

structure.help: Non-email account identifier (handle, login, employee id) when one is present alongside the credential.
structure.label: Affected username

structure.help: Email domain or service domain the exposed accounts belong to. Typically your org's domain plus any subsidiary or vendor domain seen in the dump.
structure.label: Domain in scope

structure.help: If the source is a structured file (CSV, JSON, txt), attach it here rather than pasting individual lines. Large dumps belong in a malware-sample attachment so MISP encrypts at rest.
structure.label: Leak dump (file)

structure.help: How exposed are the credentials? A bare email list is much less severe than usable cleartext password pairs.
structure.label: Severity context

structure.help: Free-form description of what was actually visible: e.g. `email + cleartext password`, `email only`, `email + bcrypt(12)`, `email + MD5`. Hash algorithm details help triage replay risk.
structure.label: Credential format

structure.help: Rough magnitude of the dump (e.g. `~12k`, `1.3M`). Free-form text rather than an integer because most operators only have an order-of-magnitude estimate at triage time.
structure.label: Approximate record count

structure.help: If this exposure traces back to a known breach, capture the linkage here so the event correlates with prior reports.
structure.label: Breach context

structure.help: Common name for the original breach (e.g. *ACME 2024*, *Collection #1*). Leave blank if unknown — speculation here corrupts correlation.
structure.label: Source breach name

structure.help: Approximate date of the underlying breach, if known. Distinct from *Date observed* above.
structure.label: Source breach date

structure.help: TLP for the report and any actor / campaign attribution you can support with evidence.
structure.label: Classification and attribution

structure.help: Pick one. Override the `tlp:amber` default if your analyst's TLP differs.
structure.label: TLP

structure.help: Optional — only fill in if your confidence is reasonable. Most credential dumps are sold on by intermediaries; direct attribution at first observation is rare.
structure.label: Suspected threat actor

structure.content: **A note on PII:** depending on jurisdiction, the affected email/username list may be subject to data-protection rules. Set the TLP and distribution accordingly, and consider whether a separate access-controlled event report is more appropriate than capturing every account inline.
